note: One list of wall controls. Admin (Wall.tsx) and Home Assistant (generated package) both follow it. Edit here first.
write_note: Writes go through wall_admin_set (p_patch). The DB merges only top-level keys (state || cleaned patch), and the cleaners rebuild each object key whole, filling anything missing with its default (ledSign, dnd, voice, alarm, radio) or dropping missing members (widgets, liveActs). So a control whose path has a dot (e.g. dnd.on, widgets.news, ledSign.notify) must read the current parent object, change that one member, and write the whole parent back. If the parent is missing, start from the defaults of its sibling controls in this file (alarm needs time, default 07:00; the admin sends on, time, days, vol 60). The same applies to dotted keys inside a button's set/also_set. widgets and liveActs: the admin writes every member each time (missing = on).

tokens.$now: Current time in ms since epoch.
tokens.$now+<ms>: Current time plus that many ms.
tokens.$inc:<path>: Current number at <path> (0 if missing) plus 1.
tokens.$nextLA:<path>: Next time (ms, rounded down to the minute) the Los Angeles clock reads the HH:MM stored at <path>; if it reads that now, the same time tomorrow.
tokens.$nextLA:<a>:after:<b>: Next time the LA clock reads <a>, counted from the next time it reads <b>.
tokens.$input:<control id>: Current value of a local (unsaved) control in this file.

fields_note: default = what the admin and wall use when the key is missing. requires = admin disables the control while that path is off. shown_if = admin hides the control unless that is true. also_set = extra keys the admin writes with every change; also_set_when_on = only when switching on. local = not in wall state, only feeds a button. needs = the control can only turn on while that path is set.
radio_note: Radio is state.radio = {on, name, url, favicon, ts} or null (the DB checks url is http(s) and at most 500 chars, name at most 60). The admin has no saved favorites and no stations table: WallRadio.tsx fetches stations live from the free Radio Browser API in the browser (de1/de2/fi1.api.radio-browser.info). 'Popular near you' = the 12 most-voted working stations within 40 km of West Hollywood (/json/stations/search?geo_lat=34.086&geo_long=-118.37&geo_distance=40000&order=votes&reverse=true&limit=24&hidebroken=true, codecs MP3/OGG/FLAC/AAC/OPUS only), plus a name search box. Tapping a station writes {on:true, name, url, favicon, ts:now}. Stop writes {...radio, on:false, ts:now} and keeps the station, and Play then brings that same station back. So HA can stop the radio any time but can only turn it on while radio.url holds a station; picking a new one needs a station url (HA could call the same Radio Browser search). The Pi plays it on the Desk HomePod. Radio and Air traffic control are exclusive: radio on sets atc false in the DB, and atc:true sent without a radio object makes the DB write radio {on:false, url:null}, which forgets the station. Right now the saved radio has url null, so there is nothing to resume until a station is picked again.

controls.label: Radio
controls.how: Off writes {...radio, on:false, ts:$now} and keeps the station. On replays the saved station ({...radio, on:true, ts:$now}) and only works while radio.url is set; the DB drops on:true without a valid url. Turning radio on also turns atc off (DB).

controls.label: Air traffic control
controls.how: Admin shows it on only when atc is true and radio.on is not. Turning it on also stops the radio: write {...radio, on:false, ts:$now} with the station kept. Sending atc:true without radio makes the DB write a radio object with url null, which forgets the station.

controls.label: Restart
controls.how: Restarts the wall page; back in about 15 seconds.

panes_note: Layout both the admin (/admin/wall) and Home Assistant follow (2026-10-04, Jared: 'as if Apple or Tesla designed it'). The top of the page is 'now': the everyday controls in the listed order. Everything else lives in a settings pane, opened from a short list of rows (title + one-line summary + chevron), Apple Settings style. A pane shows its groups in order. Every control still belongs to exactly one group; panes only decide where a group is shown.

now.note: Power (Turn on / Turn off), status and Scout's one thing sit above these in a hero card. DND buttons show contextually (quiet buttons while sounds are allowed, allow buttons while it's quiet, Back on the schedule while an override is active).
